summary_paragraph: A male patient with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and chronic systolic heart failure was admitted for periumbilical abdominal pain, weakness, dizziness, and hiccups. Initial concern for cardiac ischemia was evaluated with serial troponins, a nuclear stress test showing transient ischemic dilatation and global hypokinesis with an ejection fraction of 41%, and subsequent cardiac catheterization revealing hypertensive heart disease without coronary artery blockages. Abdominal pain was attributed to diabetic gastroparesis. The patient underwent scheduled hemodialysis, remained hemodynamically stable, and had medication adjustments including reduced doses of furosemide, losartan, and sevelamer, along with a switch to Hexavitamin. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue dialysis, monitor for recurring symptoms, and adhere to his updated medication regimen.
